writeup.p: S08 is the server's authoritative position and rotation correction: three doubles, two floats and a byte bitmask of relative flags (0x01 X, 0x02 Y, 0x04 Z, 0x08 Y_ROT, 0x10 X_ROT). It fires on join, dimension change, /tp-style teleports and anti-cheat lag-backs, and the client must answer with a C06PacketPlayerPosLook confirm or the server keeps its own position and re-sends. It is the most-intercepted clientbound packet in the corpus: every movement exploit family reads it, and several non-movement modules use it as a state signal (spawned, flagged, respawned).

NetHandlerPlayClient.handlePlayerPosLook (Memeware copy, line 601) checks PacketThreadUtil, adds each absolute field to the current value when the matching relative flag is set, calls setPosition, then immediately replies C06PacketPlayerPosLook using the bounding-box minY as the feet position. The motion zeroing lines are commented out in the Memeware and Nekoware copies, a decompile artifact of the 1.5.2-era base. The first S08 flips doneLoadingTerrain, which is the spawned signal Memeware's Stealer waits for to clear its chest state.

Five families. Flight modes cancel S08 to avoid being snapped back and re-send a confirm that matches the spoofed position (Rise MineLandFlight, CreativeFlight; Sigma Fly; Spicy Fly and BackupFly; Tenacity FlightModule). Speed modules treat S08 as a flag and auto-disable or cancel per-mode (Memeware and Nekoware Flag Check, Rise 5.99 Speed Zonecraft and Vulcan2). Rotation strippers rewrite yaw and pitch before the vanilla handler runs (Rise 5.99 NoRot and Freelook, Sigma NoRotate). Phase and Blink count or suppress teleports (Rise VulcanPhase, Sigma Phase and Blink, Spicy Phase). AntiVoid and Disabler suites use S08 as a timing trigger (Spicy AntiVoid, Rise VerusCustomDisabler and WatchdogDisabler, Sigma Disabler, Tenacity DisablerModule, Memeware Disabler Sloth mode). Sigma AntiVelocity even rewrites S08 rotations in AACFlag mode while hurtResistantTime is active. The two new clients fit the same landscape: November's PhaseModule reads S08 as its setback timer, LiquidSense's LagBack auto-disables movement modules on S08, and Tp and TeleportCommand use the teleport as their arm signal.

The anti-cheat's blunt instrument is the rubberband: any server-side position desync ends in an S08. Clients fight it three ways: cancel the packet and re-send a spoofed C06 (keeps the client position, desyncs the server), accept the position but strip rotations (NoRotate), or ignore S08 only while a module state machine is armed (VulcanPhase counts teleports and then stands down after four). Rise 6.x TeleportCheck sits on the same packet to detect teleport exploits aimed at its own users. Every anti-cheat measures the C06 echo: the confirm must match the teleported coordinates, which is why cancel-and-spoof is only viable when the module replays the exact S08 position and why repeated cancels read as teleport-spam flags.

overview: The server's authoritative position correction: doubles plus floats plus a relative-flag bitmask, answered by a mandatory C06 confirm. The most-modded clientbound packet in the corpus: Flight cancels it, Speed treats it as a flag, NoRotate strips rotation, Phase counts it, AntiVoid uses it to time its rescue, and the disabler suites use it to re-arm ping-spoof and blink state.
server_handling: NetHandlerPlayServer.setPlayerLocation (Spicy and Tenacity copies, line 448) computes the absolute target, adds the relative offsets when flags are set, zeroes the player's motion and sends S08. processPlayer validates incoming C0x movement against the last sent position and re-sends S08 when the client drifts beyond tolerance, which is the rubberband. Vanilla 1.8.9 has no teleport-id counter, so the server trusts the next C06-style confirm and re-sends S08 only when subsequent movement disagrees; that gap is exactly what cancel-and-confirm spoofing exploits.
protocol_notes: Wire order: x, y, z doubles, yaw, pitch floats, then one flags byte read via readUnsignedByte. Flagged fields are deltas added to the current client value, so the server can nudge a player with a partial teleport; the join S08 is absolute (empty flag set). The client replies with C06PacketPlayerPosLook (absolute position, bounding-box minY, current rotations, onGround flag) regardless of which fields were relative. Because the reply uses the client's post-processing position, any module that mutates the packet before the handler runs changes what the server records.
anticheat_landscape: S08 is where lag-back lands: speed, phase, ground and fly checks all terminate in one. Cancelling S08 without echoing the position forces the server into a re-send loop that is itself visible as teleport spam. The stealthy pattern is to accept the position and neutralize the effect: NoRotate rewrites rotation so the confirm matches while aim stays client-side, and disablers re-arm PingSpoofComponent immediately after S08 (Rise VerusCustomDisabler sets disable = -20 on every teleport and only spoofs once the position history is clean). Hypixel-era flight modes cancel S08 only until the server velocity-confirms the fall, then let the teleport through to avoid a permanent desync flag.

modules.name: Flight / Fly
modules.purpose: Keep a spoofed airborne position by cancelling S08 teleports until the server confirms the fall, then accept the snap-back and slow the game clock.
modules.how_it_works: On PacketReceiveEvent, cancel S08 while the module has not been teleport-confirmed; keep broadcasting C03 packets and pin the client position to the launch point. The confirm is the S12 velocity packet: once motionY passes a threshold, teleported flips true, S08 is let through and timerSpeed drops to 0.3.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Cancelling rubberbands is the classic flight flag; the MineLand pattern defuses it by accepting the teleport the moment the server's own velocity check confirms the fall, so the client is never in a permanently-desynced state.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 Fly marks a setback on S08 in Hypixel and Hycraft modes; Rise 6.2.4 CreativeFlight tracks S08 into serverPos fields to replay the teleport through its own position buffer; Sigma Fly and Spicy Fly and BackupFly cancel S08 in Hypixel mode only; Tenacity FlightModule (Mineland Fling mode) cancels S08 until the S12 confirm and then sets timer speed to 1. LiquidSense Dev's core Fly handles S08 per mode (line 761 of Fly.java), and LastestHypixelFly cancels C03 until the first S08 arms the fly window, then toggles off on a second S08 after 1500 ms with a Setback detected notice; Flight1 imports S08 without handling it.

modules.name: Speed
modules.purpose: Treat S08 as a lag-back flag and disable the module, or cancel the teleport per server mode so the speed boost survives.
modules.how_it_works: Memeware and Nekoware hook PacketInEvent: if the packet is S08 and the Flag Check setting is on, print a chat message and toggle the module off. Rise 5.99 Speed runs per-mode handlers: Zonecraft cancels S08 and re-sends C04, Vulcan2 cancels teleports inside 10 blocks, Hypixel2 cancels once, Minemenclub Hop resets its balance counter.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Auto-disable on S08 is the safest reaction because a teleport means the speed boost was already flagged; the chat message is a tell that the module was active, but the server only sees the movement it already flagged.
modules.variations: Nekoware v1 ships the identical Speed.java with the same Flag Check. Rise 5.99 adds the disableOnFlag setting that toggles the module off with a notification on any S08. LiquidSense Dev's Speed lagback check rewrites S08 yaw and pitch to the client's current rotation, zeroes motionX and motionZ and opens a stop-tick window; BufferSpeed cancels or handles S08 at its line 224.

modules.name: Disabler
modules.purpose: Use S08 as the trigger to re-arm spoofing windows, strip rotations, or nudge the teleport position to break server-side state checks.
modules.how_it_works: Rise 6.x VerusCustomDisabler sets disable = -20 on every S08 and re-arms PingSpoofComponent.spoof only after the position history is clean, holding C00 and C0F for 9 seconds. Memeware Disabler in Sloth mode adds 1.0E-4 to the S08 y to trip a spigot PlayerData nulling bug. Sigma Disabler rewrites S08 yaw and pitch and toggles itself off after the Hypixel watchdog window.
modules.vanilla_hook: PacketReceiveEvent; re-arm via PingSpoofComponent.spoof from PostStrafeEvent.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Correlating the spoof window to S08 arrivals keeps the buffered packet stream aligned with the server's position state, which is what makes the frozen-window pattern hard to distinguish from genuine lag.
modules.variations: Memeware 7.3 Sloth mode mutates the y by 1.0E-4 (spigot PlayerData exploit); Sigma 4.11 rewrites rotations and auto-disables after the Hypixel watchdog window; Rise 6.2.4 adds WatchdogDisabler alongside VerusCustomDisabler; Tenacity 6.0 keeps only commented S08 code in AdvancedDisablerModule, and Spicy and Nekoware reference S08 as imports without handling it.

modules.name: NoRotate
modules.purpose: Prevent servers from forcing the player's rotation: overwrite the S08 yaw and pitch with the client's current values before the vanilla handler applies them.
modules.how_it_works: Rise 5.99 NoRot stores the server rotation and overwrites the packet fields per mode: Vanilla replaces both fields, Delay replays the saved rotation on the next PreMotion, Legit applies it only if the mouse has not moved since. Sigma 4.11 NoRotate does the same unconditionally on incoming S08.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The confirm echoes the rewritten rotation, so the server records the client's real aim; servers that enforce rotation on teleport (some kit servers) will loop teleports, which is why the Legit mode exists.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 Freelook also rewrites S08 rotations in its camera handling; Sigma 4.11 has no restore path and no mode switch.

modules.name: Phase / Blink
modules.purpose: Suppress the block push and track teleport pressure: S08 packets are counted as the server's attempt to eject the player from a block.
modules.how_it_works: Rise 6.x VulcanPhase increments teleportCount on every S08 and stands its state machine down after four, letting blocks push the player out; it also cancels PushOutOfBlockEvent and fakes onGround = false while inside a block. Sigma Phase and Blink handle S08 on their packet bus to mask teleports during blink windows.
modules.vanilla_hook: PacketReceiveEvent; BlockAABBEvent and PushOutOfBlockEvent for the collision side.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Fighting the eject teleport directly is a permanent-flag loop; counting teleports and self-disabling after a threshold is the pattern that survives because the server eventually succeeds and the module is already off.
modules.variations: Sigma 4.11 Phase and Blink read S08 on EventPacket; Spicy Phase imports S08 without handling it in the shipped build. November Recode 2.0's PhaseModule in CAGE_PHASE mode resets its setback timer on every S08 and refuses to phase until 20 ticks pass without one; it also cancels outgoing packets while the cage window is open and flushes them on disable.

modules.name: AntiVoid
modules.purpose: Use the S08 teleport as the rescue signal: when the server lag-backs the falling player, reset fallDistance so the server's own teleport becomes the save.
modules.how_it_works: Spicy AntiVoid in Hypixel mode hooks EventPacket: on S08 while off ground, past fallDistance 20 (or below y = 0) and over void, it zeroes fallDistance. The EventUpdate path then bounces once per fall with a C03 onGround and a C04 at posY + 12. Rise VulcanAntiVoid clears its noBlock flag on S08 to re-arm the jump suppression.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventPacket (pre, incoming); EventUpdate for the bounce.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Zeroing fallDistance on the teleport is invisible to the anti-cheat because the packet is not mutated and nothing extra is sent; the module rides the server's own lag-back. Over-triggering is guarded by the isOverVoid ray scan and the bounced flag.
modules.variations: Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 VulcanAntiVoid use S08 only to re-arm the noBlock state that suppresses the jump motion while over void.

modules.name: LagBack
modules.purpose: Auto-disable movement modules when the server rubberbands, so a flagged boost quits before the anti-cheat accumulates a ban.
modules.how_it_works: On S08, gated by a 2000 ms delay, check whether Speed, LongJump, Fly, Flight or Step is toggled and the player is pressing a movement key; toggle the offending module off and print a colored chat notice per module.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Self-disabling on the first rubberband is the same strategy as Memeware's Flag Check: the server already flagged the movement, so the module quits instead of fighting the teleport.
modules.variations: Only LiquidSense Dev in the corpus; the eight original clients fold this behavior into Speed and Fly as flag-check settings.

modules.name: Teleport / Tp
modules.purpose: Use the server's own lag-back as the arm signal: cancel all C03 until S08 arrives, then walk the computed path with C04s.
modules.how_it_works: onEnable provokes the lag-back with C0F(0,-1,false), a flying-abilities C13 and C04 +0.17/+0.06. While !tp every C03 is cancelled; the first S08 flips tp and the tick handler replays the fall ladder and walks the PathfindingUtils path with per-vec3 C04s, finishing with C03(true) and C0C input.
modules.vanilla_hook: PacketEvent (S08 and C03), TickEvent (path walk), MoveEvent (cancel while waiting).
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Riding the server's own teleport as the start signal means the module never moves before the server confirms the player position, which avoids the classic teleport-spam flag.
modules.variations: TeleportCommand (LiquidSense Dev) rewrites S08 yaw and pitch to the client's rotation after a damage-ladder teleport and clears its tryCancelPacket flag; the C03 impl documents the same file family.

general_hooks: PacketReceiveEvent on every client, with the vanilla handler applying the mutation afterwards. Rise 6.x processes S08 in components (PingSpoofComponent, EntityTickComponent, TeleportCheck security) before modules see it.
client_variations: Classic clients (Memeware, Nekoware, Sigma, Spicy) mutate or cancel the packet object inside the event, so the vanilla handler then applies the modified values. Rise 5.99 and 6.x call event.setCancelled on the receive event; Rise 6.x additionally re-arms component state (PingSpoofComponent spoof windows) from the same packet.
